#### The Tragedy of Compaq

- When Compaq acquired DEC for its $13 billion revenue but inherited its unutilized Unix technology and struggling server business, the acquisition became a liability.
  - *→ hendershot cellar (organs):* so my hendershot_cellar should also document the cost of holding unused capabilities, like Compaq's DEC acquisition.
- When Compaq charged a 67% premium over Gateway 2000 systems while investing only 4% in R&D, they became beholden to external partners and lost market share.
- When Compaq refused to adopt direct sales to avoid alienating distributors, they missed the shift to commoditized PC pricing that Dell exploited.

#### The Dassler Bross: The Family Feud That Created Adidas and Puma

- When the Dassler brothers failed to adapt to casual sneaker culture, it allowed Nike to dominate the market — so focusing on athletic performance over consumer aesthetics creates vulnerability to market shifts.
  - *→ doorstep (organs):* so my doorstep organ should also monitor casual sneaker market trends
- When Adidas and Puma refused buyout offers to remain German brands, it prolonged their rivalry until personal animosity faded — so business identity tied to national pride can sustain conflict longer than market realities.
- When Adi Dassler repurposed discarded military equipment and built a bicycle-powered machine during shortages, it created the first functional products under scarcity — so resourcefulness in material constraints drives innovation.

#### Why China's Intelligence Agency is so Brutal

- When MSS operatives crossed into Hong Kong to abduct dissidents without legal procedures, they violated international law, so overseas abductions became a standard method to suppress dissent.
